properties.region: Brie and east to the Meuse
properties.smell_notes: Cream, butter, mushroom and damp woodland
properties.story_text: A 36 cm wheel of raw milk with a white rind streaked red. The largest area of the eight, about 16,300 km², stretching far east of Meaux to the Meuse, where the big dairies grew in the 19th century. 4th of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield tested.
properties.taste: Cream, butter and hazelnut (from the specification)
properties.drink: Brut Champagne, a Burgundy or Loire red, cider
properties.bread: Seeded baguette, fig or raisin bread, sourdough

properties.smell_notes: Mushroom and cabbage, stronger as it runs
properties.story_text: The exception at the top: a bloomy rind, never washed, yet 2nd of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield measured, and the highest position score of all (78). Raw milk only; generic "camembert" made anywhere does not count. Its area overlaps Pont-l'Évêque's and swallows Livarot's whole.
properties.taste: Milky (butter, cream) and barnyard, turning to mushroom and undergrowth when ripe to the core
properties.drink: Pays d'Auge cider, Pommeau or Champagne; Chinon, Beaujolais or Gevrey-Chambertin
properties.bread: Brioche, country bread, bread with candied apple and walnuts

properties.smell_notes: Sharp, peppery blue; the smell is in the veins, not the rind
properties.story_text: The first cheese with an appellation of origin, by law in 1925. The milk comes from Lacaune ewes over a wide area of the southern Massif Central, but every Roquefort ripens for at least 90 days in the caves of one commune, under the Combalou. The blue veins are Penicillium roqueforti. 5th of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield tested.
properties.taste: Rich and salty, with a sharp tang from the blue
properties.drink: A sweet white (moelleux), Port or Banyuls; amber beer
properties.bread: Nut, fig or pear bread; gingerbread
properties.food: Walnuts, hazelnuts, figs, pears, quince paste; endive

properties.region: Normandy (Calvados, Orne, Manche, part of Eure)
properties.smell_notes: Damp cellar and hay; louder at the rind than in the paste
properties.story_text: The smelliest AOP cheese by measurement: 1st of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield tested. Oddly, its specification calls the rind bloomy, which may then be brushed or washed. Square, to tell it apart from its neighbour Livarot. Its area covers some 1,300 communes, most of old Lower Normandy.
properties.taste: Mild and smooth: milk, butter, nuts, sometimes a little smoke
properties.drink: Cotentin brut cider, Pommeau, a Meursault or a Pomerol; IPA or stout

properties.smell_notes: Sweaty and meaty from the rind, mild inside
properties.story_text: One cheese, two names, both sides of a mountain range: Munster on the Alsace side, Géromé (from Gérardmer) on the Lorraine side. Regular washing feeds the red bacteria that turn the rind ivory-orange to orange-red. 3rd of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield tested.
properties.taste: Supple and melting under a loud rind: milky, hay, ripe fruit, nuts, a little yeast
properties.drink: Gewurztraminer or Pinot gris; amber beer
properties.bread: Country bread, raisin or fig bread
properties.food: Cumin seeds (some Munster has them in the paste); quiches, omelettes, pies

properties.washed_with: brine, increasingly laced with marc de Bourgogne
properties.smell_notes: Farmyard and brandy over a rind that turns brick red
properties.story_text: Named on 21 of the 24 lists, more than any other cheese. During ripening the rind is washed one to three times a week in brine that gets stronger in marc de Bourgogne, the local grape brandy. The twist: in the one measured test, the electronic nose and 19 human sniffers put it 9th of the 11 AOP cheeses they tried.
properties.taste: Creamy and melting, undergrowth and dried fruit; barnyard notes grow as it ripens
properties.drink: A Burgundy red or dry Burgundy white; amber beer
properties.bread: Wholemeal or rye; gingerbread if you are feeling bold

properties.smell_notes: Smoky and animal, powerful and long
properties.story_text: Nicknamed "the Colonel" for the strips of sedge that circle it like a colonel's stripes. Since 2017 only milk from Normande cows qualifies. The Pays d'Auge area, 290 communes, sits entirely inside both the Camembert and Pont-l'Évêque areas. 7th of the 11 AOP cheeses Cranfield tested.
properties.taste: Straw and hay, turning smoky and animal with age
properties.drink: Abbey or amber beer, Calvados, Pommeau; a Pomerol, Pommard or Vouvray

properties.smell_notes: Cellar, damp brick and undergrowth, a touch of ammonia (from the AOP specification)
properties.story_text: Its specification spells out the smell: cellar, damp brick and undergrowth, slightly ammoniated. Square and red-orange, from the Thiérache on the Belgian border. The smallest area of the eight, about 2,100 km². Cranfield did not test it.
properties.taste: Milky and slightly salty, with some acidity in the paste (from the specification)
properties.drink: Amber beer, a Burgundy or Bordeaux red, Pommeau
properties.bread: Sourdough, bread with lardons, country bread
